authorization-ownership.title: A trusted identity still needs object permission
authorization-ownership.summary: Alice/red requests a private object. Tenant matching is required before owner/reader and action checks; denial returns no private payload.

nodes.label: Request: document ID
nodes.description: Untrusted request selects a target.

nodes.label: Trusted Alice/red principal
nodes.description: Authentication adapter, not request JSON, establishes identity.

nodes.label: Tenant match
nodes.description: Object must belong to red.

nodes.label: Owner/action policy
nodes.description: Owner read/update or reader read only.

nodes.label: Denied: no private data
nodes.description: Missing/foreign/unsupported paths fail.

nodes.label: Allowed copied document
nodes.description: Only the authorized object data crosses the boundary.

steps.title: Establish identity
steps.explanation: Caller fields cannot create the principal. A trusted adapter supplies Alice/red before policy evaluation.

steps.title: Check tenant first
steps.explanation: Alice/red requesting c in blue is denied even if its owner is named Alice.

steps.title: Check object and action
steps.explanation: Within red, Bob b is denied to Alice; Alice a is granted. A reader gets read only, not update.

sessions.title: Rotate, expire and revoke server session state
sessions.summary: The fixture uses a local dictionary and injected time. Its five-minute expiry is a teaching policy, not a universal lifetime.

nodes.label: Authenticated fixture principal
nodes.description: Identity is already established by a trusted adapter.

nodes.label: Login and rotation
nodes.description: Generate a new random opaque ID; invalidate the old ID.

nodes.label: Stored session expiry
nodes.description: Login at 1 records expiry at 301.

nodes.label: Valid lookup at 300
nodes.description: The current ID remains usable before expiry.

nodes.label: Denied at 301
nodes.description: The exact expiry boundary rejects use.

nodes.label: Logout revocation
nodes.description: Remove server authority for the session.

steps.title: Rotate authority
steps.explanation: Login creation is not credential verification; rotation makes the prior bearer ID unusable.

steps.title: Test exact time boundaries
steps.explanation: Injected time verifies success at 300 and failure at 301 without sleeping.

steps.title: Revoke server state
steps.explanation: Logout must invalidate authority rather than only clear a display flag; shared storage remains an extension.

csrf.title: A mutation needs several independent gates
csrf.summary: The lesson route contract establishes session, CSRF policy, object authorization and allowed fields before mutation. Denials must preserve state.

nodes.label: Mutation request
nodes.description: Browser credentials alone do not establish deliberate intent.

nodes.label: Valid session
nodes.description: Establish current authenticated context.

nodes.label: CSRF decision
nodes.description: Verify the session-bound token and framework/origin policy.

nodes.label: Object action permission
nodes.description: Authorize this principal for this resource and action.

nodes.label: Allowed-field validation
nodes.description: Validate the narrow title-update contract.

nodes.label: Mutation and audit
nodes.description: Apply only the permitted change and record safe outcome.

nodes.label: Denied with unchanged state
nodes.description: Failed gates leave the persisted object untouched.

steps.title: Establish request context
steps.explanation: Expired sessions and wrong or cross-session tokens must fail.

steps.title: Authorize the concrete object
steps.explanation: A matching token does not grant ownership or stop same-origin XSS.

steps.title: Verify effects and denied state
steps.explanation: The local HTTP extension checks denied status and unchanged SQLite rows; browser behavior remains separate evidence.

oauth-roles.title: Trace code issuance to protected API access
oauth-roles.summary: The client, authorization server and resource server have distinct responsibilities. This conceptual flow is not executed by the offline fixture.

nodes.label: Resource owner
nodes.description: The learner participates in the provider authorization flow.

nodes.label: Notebook client
nodes.description: Requests access for the document API.

nodes.label: Authorization server
nodes.description: Processes authorization and returns a code.

nodes.label: Token endpoint
nodes.description: Redeems code plus applicable proof under provider policy.

nodes.label: Document API
nodes.description: Receives an access token for its intended audience.

nodes.label: Validation and object policy
nodes.description: Validate token, map identity and authorize document action.

steps.title: Identify participant roles
steps.explanation: OAuth access does not by itself establish the client login identity contract.

steps.title: Redeem under provider rules
steps.explanation: Do not invent validation by decoding a token; use maintained provider mechanisms.

steps.title: Authorize the API object
steps.explanation: Access token scope and a provider login are not substitutes for document ownership policy.

oidc-login.title: Verified identity must be mapped before object policy
oidc-login.summary: The opt-in OIDC adapter verifies the identity response. The synthetic Principal constructor begins after that real authentication boundary.

nodes.label: OIDC identity response
nodes.description: An ID token is intended for the configured client.

nodes.label: Maintained client validator
nodes.description: Validate metadata, key and applicable claim/correlation rules.

nodes.label: Verified issuer and subject
nodes.description: Stable identity retains its issuer context.

nodes.label: Internal account mapping
nodes.description: Map the trusted identity to an internal principal and tenant.

nodes.label: Document policy
nodes.description: Decide the requested action on the particular object.

nodes.label: Rejected identity response
nodes.description: Unverified or invalid claims cannot create a principal.

steps.title: Validate for the client
steps.explanation: Decoded payloads are not verified identity and an ID token is not a universal API bearer token.

steps.title: Map issuer and subject
steps.explanation: Email can change; use the issuer contract and an explicit account/tenant mapping.

steps.title: Keep authorization separate
steps.explanation: Successful login does not establish document ownership. The optional provider integration supplies its own negative tests.

pkce-state.title: Correlation and code redemption protect different boundaries
pkce-state.summary: Use the chosen library and provider contract. This diagram restates the training flow without implementing cryptography or live requests.

nodes.label: Flow initiation
nodes.description: Library stores per-request correlation and verifier.

nodes.label: Authorization request
nodes.description: Send S256 challenge, state and OIDC nonce as applicable.

nodes.label: Callback correlation
nodes.description: Client/library checks returned request context.

nodes.label: Code redemption
nodes.description: Send code and per-flow verifier to token endpoint.

nodes.label: Identity validation
nodes.description: Client validates ID token and required nonce.

nodes.label: Rejected flow
nodes.description: Wrong verifier, reused code or mismatched correlation fails at its owning boundary.

steps.title: Prepare separate proofs
steps.explanation: PKCE proof, callback state and OIDC nonce have distinct roles.

steps.title: Check callback before redemption
steps.explanation: The client rejects mismatched correlation; the authorization server owns code/proof redemption checks.

steps.title: Observe real denials
steps.explanation: Negative evidence belongs to the actual library/provider integration; local policy tests do not prove PKCE.

token-validation.title: Token syntax is not trusted API identity
token-validation.summary: Use a maintained validator configured for the API token format and purpose; opaque tokens follow the provider mechanism.

nodes.label: Untrusted bearer token
nodes.description: Decoding JSON or base64 is not validation.

nodes.label: Configured validator
nodes.description: Use trusted key/issuer sources and allowed algorithms.

nodes.label: Audience, lifetime and purpose
nodes.description: Signature success alone does not establish the API contract.

nodes.label: Trusted minimal claims
nodes.description: Only successfully validated claims enter mapping.

nodes.label: Principal and object policy
nodes.description: Map internal identity, then authorize the action.

nodes.label: Denied validation
nodes.description: Wrong issuer/audience, expiry, tampering or purpose cannot pass.

steps.title: Use trusted configuration
steps.explanation: A token cannot select its own arbitrary algorithm or key destination.

steps.title: Check more than the signature
steps.explanation: A signed token for another audience or issuer still fails.

steps.title: Apply business authorization
steps.explanation: Validated minimal claims are mapped before object policy. The offline kit implements none of these cryptographic checks.

secrets.title: Rotation includes consumers and old-value revocation
secrets.summary: The lesson keeps raw secret values out of evidence. A source deletion or rollback must not reactivate compromised authority.

nodes.label: Create replacement
nodes.description: Use the issuing provider or secret manager lifecycle.

nodes.label: Deploy consumers
nodes.description: Move dependent components under a defined overlap policy.

nodes.label: Verify new value
nodes.description: Observe legitimate use and relevant failure cases.

nodes.label: Revoke old value
nodes.description: Confirm the old credential no longer grants access.

nodes.label: Safe audit evidence
nodes.description: Record sanitized versions, case IDs and outcomes.

steps.title: Plan the transition
steps.explanation: Rotation changes both the credential and the consumers that depend on it.

steps.title: Verify before completing revocation
steps.explanation: Use the supported provider lifecycle and document overlap/failure policy.

steps.title: Preserve safe evidence
steps.explanation: Do not log raw values. Rollback cannot silently re-enable a compromised key.
